Generalized IRT residual-based DIF detection framework for multiple groups (GRDIF)

Source: R/grdif.R, R/print.R
grdif.Rd

This function computes three GRDIF statistics, \(GRDIF_{R}\), \(GRDIF_{S}\), and \(GRDIF_{RS}\), for analyzing differential item functioning (DIF) among multiple groups (Lim et al., 2024). They are designed mainly to detect uniform DIF, nonuniform DIF, and mixed DIF, respectively.

Usage

grdif(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
grdif(
  x,
  data,
  score = NULL,
  group,
  focal.name,
  D = 1,
  alpha = 0.05,
  missing = NA,
  purify = FALSE,
  purify.by = c("grdifrs", "grdifr", "grdifs"),
  max.iter = 10,
  min.resp = NULL,
  post.hoc = TRUE,
  method = "ML",
  range = c(-5, 5),
  norm.prior = c(0, 1),
  nquad = 41,
  weights = NULL,
  ncore = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'est_irt'
grdif(
  x,
  score = NULL,
  group,
  focal.name,
  alpha = 0.05,
  missing = NA,
  purify = FALSE,
  purify.by = c("grdifrs", "grdifr", "grdifs"),
  max.iter = 10,
  min.resp = NULL,
  post.hoc = TRUE,
  method = "ML",
  range = c(-5, 5),
  norm.prior = c(0, 1),
  nquad = 41,
  weights = NULL,
  ncore = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'est_item'
grdif(
  x,
  group,
  focal.name,
  alpha = 0.05,
  missing = NA,
  purify = FALSE,
  purify.by = c("grdifrs", "grdifr", "grdifs"),
  max.iter = 10,
  min.resp = NULL,
  post.hoc = TRUE,
  method = "ML",
  range = c(-5, 5),
  norm.prior = c(0, 1),
  nquad = 41,
  weights = NULL,
  ncore = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'grdif'
print(x, digits = max(2L, getOption("digits") - 5L), ...)

Arguments

x

A data frame containing item metadata (e.g., item parameters, number of categories, IRT model types, etc.), or an object of class est_irt or est_item obtained from est_irt() or est_item(). All items must be dichotomous ("1PLM", "2PLM", "3PLM", or "DRM"); the function stops when any item is polytomous.

See est_irt() or simdat() for more details about the item metadata. This data frame can be easily created using the shape_df() function.

...

Additional arguments passed to est_score() when abilities are estimated internally, for example tol or se. The est_score() arguments max.iter and missing cannot be passed this way, because the function uses arguments with these names for its own purposes.

data

A matrix of examinees' scored responses (0 or 1) to the dichotomous items specified in the x argument. Rows represent examinees and columns represent items.

score

A numeric vector of examinees' ability estimates (theta values), in the same row order as data. The estimates should be based on the item parameters in x (see Details). If NULL, abilities are estimated internally with est_score() using method, range, norm.prior, nquad, weights, and ncore. When purify = TRUE, abilities are re-estimated internally at every purification iteration, so a supplied score is used only in the initial analysis. A missing value in score excludes the examinee from the analysis, also during purification, with a warning. The est_item method has no score argument; it uses the abilities stored in the object. Default is NULL.

group

A numeric or character vector of examinees' group membership, with one element per row of data. It should contain the value of the reference group and the values in focal.name. Examinees whose value is not in focal.name form the reference group, and the function stops when they have more than one value. Examinees with NA in group are excluded from the analysis.

focal.name

A numeric or character vector of the values in group that identify the focal groups, with at least one value. For example, given group = c(0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3), where '0' indicates the reference group and '1', '2', and '3' indicate three focal groups, set focal.name = c(1, 2, 3). The order of focal.name determines the order of the focal groups in the results (for example, the columns n.foc1, n.foc2, and n.foc3); the GRDIF statistics do not depend on it. All examinees whose group value is not in focal.name form the reference group (see Details). Each value must be found in group, and the values must be distinct.

D

A scaling constant used in IRT models to make the logistic function closely approximate the normal ogive function. A value of 1.702 is commonly used for this purpose. Default is 1.

alpha

A numeric value specifying the significance level (\(\alpha\)) of the tests. An item is flagged by a statistic when its p-value is less than or equal to alpha. The comparison uses unrounded p-values, although the p-values reported in dif_stat are rounded to four decimal places. The same level is used in the post-hoc pairwise analyses, without an adjustment for multiple comparisons. Default is 0.05.

missing

A value indicating missing responses in the data set. Default is NA.

purify

Logical. Indicates whether to apply a purification procedure. Default is FALSE.

purify.by

A character string specifying the GRDIF statistic used for purification: "grdifrs" for \(GRDIF_{RS}\), "grdifr" for \(GRDIF_{R}\), or "grdifs" for \(GRDIF_{S}\). Used only when purify = TRUE. Default is "grdifrs".

max.iter

A positive integer specifying the maximum number of iterations allowed for the purification process. Default is 10. Each iteration removes one item, so max.iter should be at least as large as the number of items expected to be flagged. If the limit is reached while flagged items remain, a warning is issued, the complete element of the purification results is FALSE, and the items flagged in the last iteration are added to the flagged items. This argument is not passed to est_score().

min.resp

A single nonnegative number, usually a positive integer, specifying the minimum number of item responses that an examinee must have to be used in the analysis. All responses of examinees with fewer than min.resp (but at least one) responses are set to NA before the ability estimation, in the initial analysis and at every purification iteration, also when score is supplied, and these examinees are excluded from the analysis. A warning reports the number of examinees excluded in the initial analysis, and one warning at the end of the purification reports the examinees excluded during it. A large min.resp can leave a group without any ability estimate in a later purification iteration, which stops the purification with a warning. If NULL, no minimum is applied. Default is NULL. See Details for more information.

post.hoc

Logical. If TRUE, post-hoc pairwise RDIF analyses are performed, for every pair of groups, on the items flagged by each GRDIF statistic. The p-values of the post-hoc analyses are not adjusted for multiple comparisons. See Details. Default is TRUE.

method

A character string indicating the scoring method used to estimate the abilities when score = NULL and in every purification iteration. Available options are:

  • "ML": Maximum likelihood estimation

  • "MLF": Maximum likelihood estimation with fences

  • "WL": Weighted likelihood estimation (Warm, 1989)

  • "MAP": Maximum a posteriori estimation (Hambleton et al., 1991)

  • "EAP": Expected a posteriori estimation (Bock & Mislevy, 1982)

The methods "EAP.SUM" and "INV.TCC" of est_score() are not supported, because they do not give an ability estimate for each response pattern. Default is "ML".

range

A numeric vector of length two specifying the lower and upper bounds of the ability scale used when abilities are estimated internally with the scoring methods "ML", "MLF", "WL", and "MAP". Default is c(-5, 5), the default of the other DIF functions.

norm.prior

A numeric vector of length two specifying the mean and standard deviation of the normal prior distribution. These values are used to generate the Gaussian quadrature points and weights. Ignored if method is "ML" or "WL". Default is c(0, 1).

nquad

An integer indicating the number of Gaussian quadrature points to be generated from the normal prior distribution. Used only when method is "EAP". Ignored for "ML", "WL", and "MAP". Default is 41.

weights

A two-column matrix or data frame containing the quadrature points (in the first column) and their corresponding weights (in the second column) for the latent variable prior distribution. The weights and points can be conveniently generated using the function gen.weight().

If NULL and method = "EAP", default quadrature values are generated based on the norm.prior and nquad arguments. Ignored if method is "ML", "WL", or "MAP".

ncore

An integer specifying the number of logical CPU cores used by est_score() when abilities are estimated internally. The test statistics themselves are not computed in parallel. Default is 1.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, the progress of the purification procedure is printed to the console. Default is TRUE.

digits

Not used; kept for consistency with the other print methods.

Value

This function returns an object of class "grdif", which is a list with the following five components:

no_purify

A list of sub-objects presenting the results of DIF analysis without a purification procedure. These include:

dif_stat

A data frame with one row per item and the columns id, grdifr, grdifs, grdifrs, p.grdifr, p.grdifs, p.grdifrs, n.ref, n.foc1, n.foc2, ..., and n.total: the item ID, the three GRDIF statistics, their p-values, the numbers of examinees in the reference group and in each focal group (in the order of focal.name) who responded to the item, and their sum. Statistics and p-values are rounded to four decimal places.

moments

A list of three data frames, mu, var, and covariance, with the null moments of the MRR and MSR of each group, computed analytically under the null hypothesis of no DIF (Lim et al., 2024, Equations 3 to 5). mu and var have the columns id, mrr.ref, msr.ref, mrr.foc1, msr.foc1, and so on, with the null means and null variances of the MRR and MSR of the reference group and of each focal group. covariance has the columns id, ref, foc1, and so on, with the null covariance between the MRR and MSR of each group.

dif_item

A list with the elements grdifr, grdifs, and grdifrs, each giving the positions (rows of x) of the items flagged by the corresponding statistic, or NULL if no item is flagged.

score

A numeric vector of the ability estimates used in the initial analysis: the supplied score, or the internal estimates when score = NULL.

post.hoc

A list with the elements by.grdifr, by.grdifs, and by.grdifrs. Each element is a data frame with the post-hoc results for the items flagged by the corresponding GRDIF statistic, with one row per item and pair of groups and the columns id, group.pair, rdifr, z.rdifr, rdifs, z.rdifs, rdifrs, p.rdifr, p.rdifs, p.rdifrs, n.ref, n.foc, and n.total, defined as in the dif_stat element of rdif(); n.ref and n.foc refer to the first and second groups in group.pair. An element is NULL if no item is flagged by the statistic or if post.hoc = FALSE.

purify

A logical value indicating whether purification was requested (the purify argument).

with_purify

A list with the results of the purification procedure. All elements are NULL when purify = FALSE. The elements are:

purify.by

A character string indicating which GRDIF statistic was used for purification: "grdifr", "grdifs", or "grdifrs", corresponding to \(GRDIF_{R}\), \(GRDIF_{S}\), and \(GRDIF_{RS}\), respectively.

dif_stat

A data frame with the same columns as no_purify$dif_stat and an additional column n.iter. For an item removed during purification, the row reports the statistics from the iteration in which the item was removed, and n.iter is that iteration minus 1 (0 for an item removed on the basis of the initial analysis). For the other items, the row reports the statistics from the last iteration, and n.iter is the number of that iteration. If no item is flagged in the initial analysis, this is no_purify$dif_stat with n.iter = 0.

moments

A list of three data frames with the same columns as in no_purify$moments and an additional column n.iter, defined in the same way as in dif_stat.

dif_item

A numeric vector of the positions (rows of x) of the items flagged by the purify.by statistic, sorted in ascending order. It contains the items removed during purification and, if max.iter is reached or the purification stops because a group has no ability estimate left, the items flagged in the last iteration (iteration n.iter). It contains all items if every item is flagged. NULL if no item is flagged in the initial analysis.

n.iter

The number of purification iterations performed (0 if no item is flagged in the initial analysis). The iteration that removes the last item, or after which a group has no ability estimate left, is not counted, because the statistics are not recomputed.

score

A numeric vector of the ability estimates from the last iteration counted in n.iter. NULL if no item is flagged in the initial analysis, because purification is not carried out; the initial estimates are then in no_purify$score.

post.hoc

A data frame with the same columns as the elements of no_purify$post.hoc and an additional column n_iter. It contains the post-hoc results of each item removed during purification, computed with the ability estimates of the iteration in which the item was removed; n_iter is defined as n.iter in dif_stat. NULL if post.hoc = FALSE or if no item is flagged in the initial analysis.

complete

A logical value. TRUE if the procedure stopped because no remaining item was flagged (including the case in which no item is flagged in the initial analysis), and FALSE if it stopped because max.iter was reached, because every item was flagged, or because a group had no examinee with an ability estimate left.

alpha

A numeric value indicating the significance level (\(\alpha\)) used for the tests.

call

The matched function call.

Details

The GRDIF framework (Lim et al., 2024) generalizes the RDIF framework (Lim & Choe, 2023; Lim et al., 2022) to more than two groups. For each item and group, the mean raw residual (MRR) and the mean squared residual (MSR) are computed, where a residual is the observed item score minus the model-expected item score evaluated at the examinee's ability estimate. Under the null hypothesis that the item has no DIF between any pair of groups, the MRRs and MSRs asymptotically follow normal distributions whose means, variances, and covariances are computed analytically from the model-predicted probabilities (Lim et al., 2024, Equations 2 to 6). \(GRDIF_{R}\), \(GRDIF_{S}\), and \(GRDIF_{RS}\) are quadratic forms of the contrasts between the focal groups and the reference group of the MRRs, of the MSRs, and of both, centered at their null means, in the inverse of their null covariance matrices (Lim et al., 2024, Equation 10). Under the null hypothesis, they asymptotically follow \(\chi^{2}\) distributions with G-1, G-1, and 2(G-1) degrees of freedom, respectively, where G is the number of groups. The statistics do not depend on which group is the reference group. For two groups, \(GRDIF_{R}\) and \(GRDIF_{S}\) equal the squares of the standardized \(RDIF_{R}\) and \(RDIF_{S}\) statistics of rdif(), \(GRDIF_{RS}\) equals \(RDIF_{RS}\), and the p-values are the same.

grdif() supports dichotomous items only, because the GRDIF framework has been developed and evaluated for dichotomous items (Lim et al., 2024). The function stops with an error when x includes any item with three or more score categories or any item of the "GRM" or "GPCM" model.

To compute the GRDIF statistics, grdif() requires: (1) item parameter estimates obtained from aggregate data (regardless of group membership), (2) examinees' ability estimates (e.g., ML), and (3) examinees' item response data. Note that the ability estimates must be based on the aggregate-data item parameters. The item parameter estimates should be provided in the x argument, the ability estimates in the score argument, and the response data in the data argument. If ability estimates are not provided (i.e., score = NULL), grdif() estimates them with the scoring method specified in the method argument (e.g., method = "ML"). When x is an object of class est_irt, the item parameter estimates, the response data, and the scaling constant D are taken from the object. When x is an object of class est_item, the ability values stored in the object are also used as score.

In rare cases, the covariance matrix of the contrasts that define \(GRDIF_{R}\), \(GRDIF_{S}\), or \(GRDIF_{RS}\) is singular or nearly singular (its reciprocal condition number is 1e-10 or less), for example when all examinees of a group who responded to an item have the same probability of a correct response, so that the MSR is a linear function of the MRR. Then the statistic is computed with the Moore-Penrose generalized inverse of the covariance matrix and compared with a chi-square distribution whose degrees of freedom equal the rank of the matrix (Moore, 1977), and one warning names the items. This handling is not part of the original method (Lim et al., 2024) and is added in irtQ. In most data the matrix is not singular, and the degrees of freedom are G-1, G-1, and 2(G-1).

The group argument contains the group membership of each examinee as numeric or character values, and its length must equal the number of rows in data. The values listed in focal.name identify the focal groups, and all other examinees form the reference group. The group vector should therefore contain one value for the reference group in addition to the values in focal.name, and the function stops when it contains more than one such value. Examinees with NA in group are excluded from the analysis.

As in the RDIF framework, an iterative purification procedure can be applied (Lim et al., 2022, 2024). When purify = TRUE, the statistic specified in purify.by drives the procedure (e.g., purify.by = "grdifrs"). At each iteration, the flagged item with the smallest p-value of the purify.by statistic is removed (the p-values are compared on the log scale), the abilities are re-estimated from the remaining items with the scoring method specified in method, and the GRDIF statistics of the remaining items are recomputed. A supplied score is therefore used only in the initial analysis. The procedure stops when no remaining item is flagged or when max.iter iterations have been performed. If no item is flagged in the initial analysis, no iteration is performed. If every item is flagged, the procedure stops with a warning, because no item is left to estimate the abilities, and complete is FALSE. The procedure also stops with a warning and complete = FALSE when, after an item is removed, no examinee of the reference group or of a focal group has an ability estimate left (see min.resp below); the remaining items then keep the results and the scores of the previous iteration, and the items flagged in that iteration are added to the flagged items.

Scoring based on a small number of item responses can lead to large standard errors, potentially reducing the accuracy of DIF detection in the GRDIF framework. The min.resp argument excludes such examinees. For example, if min.resp = 5, examinees who responded to fewer than five items (but at least one) have all their responses treated as missing (i.e., NA) before the abilities are estimated, in the initial analysis and at every purification iteration, and a warning reports their number in the initial analysis. As a result, their ability estimates are missing, and they are not used in the computation of the GRDIF statistics. When score is supplied, the scores of these examinees are also treated as missing. During purification, the count is based on the items that remain after the flagged items are removed, and an examinee excluded once stays excluded. If min.resp = NULL, a score is computed for any examinee with at least one valid item response.

Examinees whose ability estimate is NA, such as examinees without any item response or examinees with NA in a supplied score, are excluded from the computation of the GRDIF statistics and from the post-hoc analyses. A warning reports the number of examinees with item responses who are excluded because of a missing value in score; these examinees stay excluded during purification. During purification, an examinee whose remaining responses are all removed with the flagged items, or who has fewer than min.resp responses to the remaining items, has no ability estimate and is excluded, and one warning at the end reports the number of such examinees. The sample sizes n.ref, n.foc1, n.foc2, and so on count only the examinees who are used.

If no examinee of one of the groups responded to an item, the GRDIF statistics and p-values of the item are NaN, and the item is not flagged.

The GRDIF statistics test only whether DIF is present between at least one pair of groups (Lim et al., 2024). When post.hoc = TRUE, the three RDIF statistics of rdif() are computed for every pair of distinct values in group, for each item flagged by \(GRDIF_{R}\), \(GRDIF_{S}\), or \(GRDIF_{RS}\). For example, with four groups A, B, C, and D, the pairs A-B, A-C, A-D, B-C, B-D, and C-D are compared. Each pairwise analysis uses the responses of the examinees in the two groups, their ability estimates from the GRDIF analysis, and the item parameters in x; the abilities are not re-estimated for the pair. In a pair labeled "a & b" in the column group.pair, a is the reference group and b is the focal group of the pair, so \(RDIF_{R}\) and \(RDIF_{S}\) are the residual means of group b minus those of group a. The reference group of the GRDIF analysis is the reference group of every pair that includes it (Lim et al., 2024, Equation 14), and for a pair of focal groups, the group listed earlier in focal.name is the reference group. The p-values are not adjusted for multiple comparisons; to control the familywise error rate, compare them with a corrected level, for example alpha divided by the number of pairs (a Bonferroni correction). When purify = TRUE, the post-hoc results in with_purify are computed for each item when it is removed during purification, with the ability estimates of that iteration; the items added to the flagged items when the purification ends before it is complete (max.iter reached or no ability estimate left in a group) are not analyzed.

The print method of this class has an argument digits that is not used; the statistics are printed rounded to three decimal places.

Methods (by class)

  • grdif(default): Default method for a data frame x containing item metadata.

  • grdif(est_irt): Method for an object of class est_irt created by est_irt(). The response data and the scaling constant D are taken from the object.

  • grdif(est_item): Method for an object of class est_item created by est_item(). The response data, the ability estimates, and the scaling constant D are taken from the object.

Methods (by generic)

  • print(grdif): Print method for an object of class grdif (given as x). It prints the flagged items and the GRDIF statistics of the analyses without and with purification, rounded to three decimal places.

Lim, H., Choe, E. M., & Han, K. T. (2022). A residual-based differential item functioning detection framework in item response theory. Journal of Educational Measurement, 59(1), 80-104. doi:10.1111/jedm.12313 .

Examples

# \donttest{
# Load required library
library("dplyr")

## Uniform DIF detection for four groups (1 reference, 3 focal)
########################################################
# (1) Manipulate uniform DIF for all three focal groups
########################################################

# Import the "-prm.txt" output file from flexMIRT
flex_sam <- system.file("extdata", "flexmirt_sample-prm.txt", package = "irtQ")

# Select 36 non-DIF items modeled under 3PLM
par_nstd <-
  bring.flexmirt(file = flex_sam, "par")$Group1$full_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$model == "3PLM") %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() %in% 1:36) %>%
  dplyr::select(1:6)
par_nstd$id <- paste0("nondif", 1:36)

# Generate four new items on which uniform DIF will be imposed
difpar_ref <-
  shape_df(
    par.drm = list(a = c(0.8, 1.5, 0.8, 1.5), b = c(0.0, 0.0, -0.5, -0.5), g = rep(0.15, 4)),
    item.id = paste0("dif", 1:4), cats = 2, model = "3PLM"
  )

# Introduce DIF by shifting b-parameters differently for each focal group
difpar_foc1 <-
  difpar_ref %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(.vars = "par.2", .funs = function(x) x + c(0.7, 0.7, 0, 0))
difpar_foc2 <-
  difpar_ref %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(.vars = "par.2", .funs = function(x) x + c(0, 0, 0.7, 0.7))
difpar_foc3 <-
  difpar_ref %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(.vars = "par.2", .funs = function(x) x + c(-0.4, -0.4, -0.5, -0.5))

# Combine the 4 DIF and 36 non-DIF items for all four groups
# Therefore, each of the first four items has uniform DIF in two of the three
# focal groups
par_ref <- rbind(difpar_ref, par_nstd)
par_foc1 <- rbind(difpar_foc1, par_nstd)
par_foc2 <- rbind(difpar_foc2, par_nstd)
par_foc3 <- rbind(difpar_foc3, par_nstd)

# Generate true abilities from different distributions
set.seed(128)
theta_ref <- rnorm(500, 0.0, 1.0)
theta_foc1 <- rnorm(500, -1.0, 1.0)
theta_foc2 <- rnorm(500, 1.0, 1.0)
theta_foc3 <- rnorm(500, 0.5, 1.0)

# Simulate response data for each group
resp_ref <- irtQ::simdat(par_ref, theta = theta_ref, D = 1)
resp_foc1 <- irtQ::simdat(par_foc1, theta = theta_foc1, D = 1)
resp_foc2 <- irtQ::simdat(par_foc2, theta = theta_foc2, D = 1)
resp_foc3 <- irtQ::simdat(par_foc3, theta = theta_foc3, D = 1)
data <- rbind(resp_ref, resp_foc1, resp_foc2, resp_foc3)

########################################################
# (2) Estimate item and ability parameters
#     using aggregated data
########################################################

# Estimate item parameters
est_mod <- irtQ::est_irt(data = data, D = 1, model = "3PLM")

#> Estimating item parameters...

#> Computing item parameter var-covariance matrix... 
#> Estimation is finished in 2.3 seconds. 
est_par <- est_mod$par.est

# Estimate ability parameters using MLE
score <- irtQ::est_score(x = est_par, data = data, method = "ML")$est.theta

########################################################
# (3) Conduct DIF analysis
########################################################

# Create a group membership vector:
# 0 = reference group; 1, 2, 3 = focal groups
group <- c(rep(0, 500), rep(1, 500), rep(2, 500), rep(3, 500))

# (a) Compute GRDIF statistics without purification,
#     and perform post-hoc pairwise comparisons for flagged items
dif_nopuri <- grdif(
  x = est_par, data = data, score = score, group = group,
  focal.name = c(1, 2, 3), D = 1, alpha = 0.05,
  purify = FALSE, post.hoc = TRUE
)
print(dif_nopuri)
